scenes.title: Turn a priority into a design
scenes.visual: Founder reviews an anonymous priority plan.
scenes.narration: You chose a learning priority. Now design a small check that can inform the next decision. An experiment design states the assumption, method, evidence and interpretation before execution. This lesson creates a plan; it does not run the experiment or validate a venture.

scenes.title: Make the hypothesis specific
scenes.visual: Editable group, context and claim cards.
scenes.narration: State a claim that could be wrong for a specific group and context. Define what decision the result affects. Checking whether instructions are understood is different from checking actual use or payment. Keep the question narrow enough that the method can answer it.

scenes.title: Choose the smallest fitting format
scenes.visual: Editable observation, prototype and manual-process cards.
scenes.narration: Choose a bounded format such as a permitted observation, a clarity task or a manual process trial. Explain why it fits and what it cannot establish. An early learning check is not automatically a controlled experiment, and a convenient sample is not representative.

scenes.title: Define signals and interpretation
scenes.visual: Editable supportive, weakening and inconclusive cards.
scenes.narration: Decide what you will observe and how you will interpret it before collecting results. Use a baseline or comparison when relevant and feasible. Explain any threshold rather than inventing a universal pass number. Include ambiguous results, alternative explanations and what the check cannot prove.

scenes.title: Set safeguards and limits
scenes.visual: Editable permission, stop and fallback cards.
scenes.narration: Confirm permission, voluntary participation, privacy and the resources needed. Keep pending access pending. State stop conditions and a fallback. Do not collect money, contact participants or record people merely because the worksheet is complete. Avoid deception and unnecessary personal information.

scenes.title: Create the experiment design
scenes.narration: Build your Small Experiment Design with the priority claim, hypothesis, method, participants, signals, interpretation rule, safeguards and review plan. Record only planned actions here, not invented findings. Next you will combine the design into a practical validation test plan.

sections.label: 02 / LEARN
sections.heading: Design for a decision, not a success story.

children: A
hypothesis
is a specific claim that could be wrong. A
method
gathers information relevant to it. A
signal
is an observable outcome. An
interpretation rule
explains what supportive, weakening or inconclusive information would mean.
Use the first priority from Lesson 23 and define group/context.
Write a testable claim and the decision it affects.
Choose a small method that fits; record its limits.
Define participants/access and selection bias.
Set signals and interpretation before collecting results.
Set permission, privacy, resources, stop conditions and review.
Illustrative design:

a voluntary directions-clarity task could check whether adults understand a proposed instruction. It does not prove real-world adoption, payment or time savings. Its setting and selection may affect results.

Use a baseline or comparison where appropriate; explain when it is absent. A learning check is not automatically a controlled experiment. Do not invent a universal sample size or passing threshold. Qualitative criteria are acceptable with reasons and limits.

Keep supportive, weakening and inconclusive paths visible. Avoid changing criteria after seeing results without recording the change. Pending permission remains pending; this prototype does not recruit, charge, record or run a test.
Review validation priority plan
